lead.label: 1a
lead.why: Abstract: 'compounds 1a and 1h exhibited enhanced inhibitory effects on USP5 ...'. Both are named together; 1a is taken because it has the lowest IC50 in Table 1 (4.38 uM vs 6.64 uM for 1h) and is listed first.

reactions.conditions: Et3N (2.0 eq), CH2Cl2, rt, 3 h; aqueous work-up gives a light yellow solid used directly.
reactions.source: Section 4.1.1, general route for 1a-1j (main text p. 7-8); Scheme 1

reactions.conditions: Hydrazine hydrate (5 mL), EtOH, reflux 80 C, 2 h; product precipitates on cooling, washed with cold EtOH.
Alkyl chloroformate (1.2 eq), DMAP (0.2 eq), THF, 0 C to rt, overnight; 92% (469.6 mg from 1.0 mmol).

notes: The paper does not print names for intermediates 6a and 7a or for the aryl piperidine (general procedure with 'aryl cycloamine compounds'); the piperidine is inferred from the name of 1a (4-(4-bromophenyl)piperidin-1-yl) and 'all reagents from commercial suppliers'. Ethyl chloroformate is inferred from the ethyl carbamate in 1a's name; the generic text says 'corresponding alkyl chloroformate'. Step 1 and 2 products are not individually characterised. Lead is 1a or 1h by the abstract; 1a chosen on IC50.
